sections.label: Retryable vs. non-retryable
items: **Retryable**: 429 (rate limit), timeouts, transient 5xx: the identical request has a real chance of succeeding on retry.
**Non-retryable**: 400 (malformed request), auth failures: identical retry fails identically, every time.

sections.label: Bounded call shape
items: Retry the primary on retryable failures, up to a fixed max.
Stop retrying immediately on a non-retryable error, don't wait out the budget.
Once primary is exhausted/blocked, try fallback exactly ONCE, not with the same generous budget.

sections.label: Why jitter, not just backoff
items: Fixed or pure-exponential delays synchronize many callers into a simultaneous retry storm.
Full jitter (random between 0 and the cap) spreads retries across a window instead of a single instant.

sections.label: Common mistakes
items: Retrying a non-retryable error until the attempt count runs out instead of failing fast.
Giving fallback the same retry budget as the primary.
Using fixed delay or exponential-without-jitter under real concurrent load.

sections.label: Implementation checklist
checklist: Retryable classification is checked independently of the attempt counter.
Primary retries are capped; fallback gets exactly one attempt.
Both primary and fallback failing returns a clear structured failure, never an uncaught exception.
